column1: Dealing With Asymmetric Information As Larry considers financing Patti’s business venture, one question is paramount in his mind: Will her company succeed? If Larry offers her equity financing, he gets a share of future profits, so the fortune of the business is crucial. Debt financing is safer for Larry, because debt holders are paid before equity holders get anything, but Patti’s success is still relevant. If the doll business is a failure, Patti may not be able to repay the loan. That is, she might default. Not only might Larry not get the interest he was promised, but he might lose his principal (the amount of the loan) as well.
